key_insight: A total-pressure formulation enables locking-free poroelastic optimal control, with first-order error estimates uniform as the Lamé parameter increases under stated regularity and positive-storage assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The method supports reliable source-control optimization in nearly incompressible porous materials while enforcing bounds on control inputs.
method: Track displacement and fluid pressure with box-constrained distributed source control.
Use a mechanical Schur complement to establish zero-storage well-posedness for each fixed finite Lamé parameter.
Discretize states and adjoints with conforming finite elements and dG(0) time stepping, using piecewise constant controls.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments confirm predicted convergence rates, examine Lamé-parameter and storage-coefficient dependence, and demonstrate localized pressure control with active bounds.
watch_item: Zero-storage well-posedness does not imply zero-storage error guarantees: the first-order estimates require a positive lower bound on storage.
paper_title: Locking-free numerical methods for poroelasticity optimal control problems with minimal regularities
